naraSticker.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: one finished horizontal travel memory sticker card.
Input images: Image 1 is the existing Nara card, the EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the Fuji card, a supporting reference ONLY for matte paper, flat color masses and quiet editorial simplification. Transfer none of its contents or words.
Primary request: Keep the Nara card's excellent finished layout, scene, six sticker shapes, overall palette and exact typography. Change ONE thing: simplify ALL illustrated contents radically from descriptive painting into deliberately clumsy flat gouache / torn cut-paper shapes. The first visual read must be 3–6 large blunt masses and generous quiet space. All contents are redrawn; none retain photographic or realistic fur texture.
Main illustration: reduce the foreground brown deer into about four broad brown/cream color planes, compact black eye marks and a blunt dark nose, preserving its signature asymmetric huge ears and tilted face. No fur hairs, fur strokes, realistic eye highlights or detailed animal anatomy. Reduce the tree and background vegetation into three lumpy olive masses with no detailed leaves. Use a nearly uninterrupted sage pond field, only two or three broad reflection shapes, no small ripples. Preserve the simple right-hand gray-roof pavilion silhouette but reduce it to a handful of big planes with only essential posts. Cherry blossoms become rough pink patches. Source identification anchor remains the large tilted deer head and asymmetric ears.
Every sticker must share this same VERY SIMPLE matte flat paper medium and coarse blunt shapes. Preserve exactly SIX stickers: full deer; deer head; pavilion; cherry branch; pond with one gray rock; fence post with rope. Keep them physically separated in the right 30–32% with thick irregular warm-white cut edges, subtle flat shadows, relaxed spacing and the current clear size hierarchy.
Invariants: one 3:2 landscape card, continuous warm off-white uncoated paper outer border; left illustration occupies 66–68% and is totally unframed, no outline, box, mat or shadow; shallow footer remains beneath the LEFT illustration on exposed paper. Keep exact text ONCE, small and centered: "Spring · Deer · Pond". No other readable text, title, signature, watermark, extra sticker, duplicate motif, separate card or object.
Material: 5–8 broad low-saturation color families, opaque matte fills, hand-cut chalky imperfect contours, fine uniform paper tooth and minimal pigment variation. Avoid all realistic texture, photographic patches, descriptive brushwork, watercolor wash, gradients, marker strokes, intricate repeated marks, polished vectors, clip art, gloss and 3D. Preserve composition and typography; simplify the drawing.

naraSticker.sourcePrompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: finished horizontal collectible travel memory sticker card for a website.
Primary request: Create ONE complete 3:2 horizontal card from the Nara deer source photo, matching the card system and quiet handmade material of the Fuji sticker-card reference.
Input images: Image 1, deer-source.png, is the SUBJECT and SCENE reference. Image 2, fuji-sticker.png, is ONLY the CARD LAYOUT and MATTE PAPER STYLE reference. Do not include Fuji, its cafe, its trees, blue-hour palette, or any of its words.
Canvas and layout: landscape 3:2. Warm off-white uncoated paper with a continuous 4–5% outer paper margin. The left 66–68% is one vertical unit: a large near-square completely UNFRAMED illustration above a shallow exposed-paper footer. The illustration rests directly on the card paper with a subtly rough edge; no outline, keyline, mat, inner card, rounded frame, shadow, or sticker edge around the main illustration. The right 30–32% contains exactly SIX separate die-cut stickers extending over the full composition height.
Main illustration: retain the source relationship of the close, curious brown deer in the foreground at left, its wide asymmetric ears and gentle compact face, pale cherry blossoms and large lumpy green tree masses above and behind it, a calm sage-colored pond behind, and the Japanese pavilion with slate-gray roof standing over the pond on the far right. The recognisable anchor is the deer's large asymmetrical ear-and-head silhouette, rendered in the same coarse matte medium as everything else. Use naive slightly clumsy proportions. Enlarge the quiet pond and pale sky fields. Rebuild the whole scene from 5–8 broad matte color families: warm dusty brown, warm cream, muted olive, pond sage, gray slate, restrained cherry pink, muted pale sky. First read must be 3–6 oversized blunt shapes and quiet space.
Style and material: opaque matte gouache and hand-cut paper color planes, fine uniform paper tooth, chalky uneven contours, subtle pigment density variation and light misregistration. Flat color shadows only. Compress vegetation into 1–3 lumpy tonal masses; pavilion into simple planes; deer into a compact simplified silhouette. No fur detail, individual detailed leaves, intricate branches or anatomy.
Right-column stickers: EXACTLY SIX distinct, physically separated source-derived motifs, each with thick irregular warm-white hand-cut border and a very subtle flat paper shadow. The six and only six are (1) one small full brown deer with compact legs, (2) one isolated deer head with the wide ears, (3) the pond pavilion, (4) one simple pink cherry-blossom branch, (5) a small sage pond patch with one gray rock, (6) one brown fence post with a short rope segment. Treat each numbered motif as ONE sticker, including the pond-plus-rock and post-plus-rope groups. Make the deer, pavilion, and blossom branch larger; other stickers smaller. Use calm staggered irregular spacing, no grid labels, no extra stickers and no duplicated motifs.
Text (verbatim): "Spring · Deer · Pond"
Text placement: those exactly three English keywords occur ONCE, centered small and quiet in muted brown ink on the exposed paper footer beneath the LEFT illustration. No box, no label, not inside the illustration, not beneath the sticker column.
Constraints: NO landmark text. No title, caption, date, subtitle, writing area, postal marks, address lines, other readable text, watermark or signature. The whole image and every sticker use one cohesive matte cut-paper/gouache grain medium; NO photographic patch anywhere. No watercolor washes or blooms, marker bands, photorealistic texture, glossy 3D, dramatic lighting, gradients, polished vector art, anime or clip art. One complete card, not a lone deer cutout, not a contact sheet, not a collage of multiple cards.

fujiDiorama.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: square product image of one assembled travel-memory papercraft miniature for a website.
Primary request: Rebuild the Fuji cafe photograph as ONE complete assembled papercraft scenery model, using the Nara deer diorama's tangible cardstock material, ivory hexagonal display base, studio background and three-quarter camera.
Input images: Image 1, fuji-postcard.png, supplies SUBJECT CONTENT from the TOP PHOTOGRAPH ONLY: snow-capped Mount Fuji behind a low dark cafe with warm windows, conifers, blue-hour mist and a lamppost. Ignore the lower illustration, lower paper section, all footer text, and the postcard's stacked composition. Image 2, deer-diorama.png, supplies only the MODEL FORMAT, cardstock material, hexagonal ivory base, complete assembled scenery presentation, soft studio lighting and three-quarter camera. Do not transfer deer, pavilion, cherry blossoms, pond, or Nara vegetation.
Composition: ONE SQUARE 1:1 image. ONE single complete assembled model centered on ONE thick ivory hexagonal base. Camera at a three-quarter isometric angle, about 30 degrees downward, comparable to the Nara diorama. The entire assembled miniature and its base occupy about 65% of the square frame, with clear calm cream studio background and enough breathing room on all four sides. The base and all objects must be fully within the frame.
Assembled scenery: a folded dimensional blue Mount Fuji with a recognisable white snow cap at the REAR of the base; a small fully assembled low rectangular charcoal cafe with amber-gold paper windows at the FRONT; exactly TWO dark blue-green conifers standing upright, one at left and one at right; a few layered pale-blue cardstock mist shapes attached at the foot of the mountain and behind the cafe; exactly ONE slender upright dark lamppost near the cafe. A simple muted blue-gray ground plane completes the integrated scenery. All elements are assembled, rooted and attached to the SAME base, with clear depth relationships. Preserve the Fuji-behind-cafe silhouette and snow/cool-blue/warm-window color relationship from the photograph. The building should read as the photo's cafe through shape and amber glazing; omit all brand lettering and logos.
Materials: tactile matte cardstock, finely fibrous cut edges, visible scored fold lines and bent paper planes, subtle glued seams, dimensional folded parts, restrained faceted paper geometry, handmade paper construction. Soft cream studio lighting and gentle contact shadows beneath the single hexagonal ivory base. Quiet blue, warm amber, charcoal and ivory palette.
Critical constraints: one assembled scene and only one scene. NO loose parts, no disassembled pieces at the bottom or anywhere, no duplicate objects, no exploded view, no flat-lay of components, no build instructions, no collage, no split image, no multiple views, no extra base, no parts inventory. Everything is already assembled on the one hexagonal base. No text, caption, logos, watermark or signature. No deer or Nara pavilion. No realistic landscape photograph, plastic toy, glossy surfaces or dramatic lighting.
